question.problem: On which of the following intervals can the intermediate value theorem be applied to the function $f(x)=\frac{x}{x-1}?$
question.worked_solution:
The intermediate value theorem can be applied to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

The function is discontinuous at the values of $x$ which make the denominator equal to zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero, we have $x-1=0,$ which corresponds to $x=1.$ 

We conclude that the intermediate value theorem can be applied to the function $f(x)$ only on closed intervals that do not contain the point $x=1.$ 

From the given options, only the interval $[-1,0]$ is allowed.  The intervals $(1,2]$ and $[-1,1)$ are not closed, $[-2,2]$ and $[0,2]$ contain the point $x=1.$
